name: protocol semantics
reason: Protocol factors with no artefact. The strong area is GraphQL and schema-driven testing, where several entries do state a procedure. The weak areas are JSON-RPC, SOAP routing, protobuf field semantics, OData and agent to agent delegation, which have nothing at all.

L03-001.note: Both recover a GraphQL schema. That is one protocol's discovery path, not the general question of how much surface is exposed.

L03-002.note: Property based testing against the declared schema finds exactly where the implementation accepts what the schema does not declare.

L03-003.note: Undeclared field acceptance is one of the properties a schema driven generator tests, with the schema as the oracle.

L03-004.note: Type mutation is generated. Whether coercion changed behaviour is not stated as the oracle.

L03-006.note: The target is explicitly built around mass assignment, so the procedure and the confirmation both exist.

L03-007.note: Replaying every request as a lower principal compares verbs on the same object, which is the parity question.

L03-011.note: Parameter fuzzing can surface pollution. Which duplicate wins is not the stated oracle.

L03-013.note: Type substitution is generated and the array in scalar position case is not named.

L03-014.note: A GraphQL security checker names field and edge authorisation as a class. The per field test is not stated.

L03-015.note: Alias and batching abuse is the whole subject of the entry, with a stated confirmation.

L03-016.note: Batch execution semantics are what the tool tests, including the multiply the checks.

L03-018.note: Both work around introspection being disabled. Whether it is truly off is not tested.

L03-021.note: Listing services from a running server is the reflection check, and the method list is the oracle.

L03-026.note: JSON number precision and identifier collision is unaddressed anywhere.

L03-027.note: Escape payloads exist per context. Whether validation happens before or after decoding is not tested.

L03-031.note: Entity expansion and external reference are the subject, with file or network read as the oracle.

L03-032.note: Signature wrapping is named explicitly, with the modified assertion accepted as the confirmation.

L03-033.note: Canonicalisation is the mechanism wrapping relies on. The entry attacks it rather than testing the two canonical forms directly.

L03-034.note: Audience checking is a stated requirement. No artefact tests a cross service assertion.

L03-039.note: A controllable identity provider makes the redirect test possible. No entry states the procedure.

L03-041.note: PKCE is a requirement in the specification entry, not a test.

L03-047.note: Run here on 2026-10-27 as obs-002. A verifier that dispatches on the token's declared alg accepted an unsigned token with role admin, while a wrong signature under HS256 was rejected with 401 and the genuine user token was refused with 403. Two controls, because this class has two ways to be wrong.

L03-048.note: Claim tampering shows the token can be changed. Whether the application revalidates the claim is the untested half.

L03-049.note: Key identifier traversal is named as part of the tool's attack set.

L03-053.note: Both drive tests from the published specification, so an undocumented live route is the finding.

L03-056.note: Scanning tool descriptions for hostile instruction is the factor as written, with a flagged description as the oracle.

L03-057.note: Tool poisoning is the named class. Authority escalation through a result is described rather than tested.

L03-058.note: A request served by a server other than the one intended is the identity and scope question.

L03-061.note: Deterministic replay can show a duplicate effect. Idempotency key handling is not the stated subject.

L03-062.note: Parameter fuzzing can edit a cursor. Whether the cursor is signed is not tested.

L03-020.note: An object loaded without the check its sibling path applies is the boundary failure.

L03-024.note: A field cleared that was meant to be left alone is the presence ambiguity.
